content.text:
gbrain init — initialize a brain (PGLite or Supabase Postgres)

USAGE
  gbrain init [flags]

ENGINE SELECTION (mutually exclusive)
  --pglite              Use embedded PGLite (zero-config, the default)
  --supabase            Use Supabase Postgres (recommended for 1000+ files)
  --url <URL>           Use a manual Postgres connection string
  --mcp-only            Thin-client mode: connect to a remote gbrain MCP, no local engine

OPTIONS
  --force               Overwrite an existing config (gated by default)
  --non-interactive     Don't prompt; use defaults
  --migrate-only        Apply pending schema migrations against the configured engine
                        without re-saving config (used by post-upgrade and orchestrators)
  --json                JSON output for status reporting
  --content-root <path> Use a new owned content directory (existing source roots win)
  --db-only             Keep memory database-only; shared publication needs export/adoption
  --git                 Authorize Git init in the new owned empty content directory
  --no-git              Keep a content directory without Git (default)
  --path <DIR>          Override default brain path (PGLite only)
  --key <APIKEY>        Provide an API key non-interactively (Supabase only)
  --embedding-model <PROVIDER:MODEL>
                        e.g. openai:text-embedding-3-large, voyage:voyage-multimodal-3
  --model <PROVIDER>    Shorthand: pick recipe default for a provider
  --embedding-dimensions <N>
                        Embedding dimensions (must match the model)
  --expansion-model <PROVIDER:MODEL>
                        Model for query expansion (default: anthropic:claude-haiku)
  --chat-model <PROVIDER:MODEL>
                        Default subagent driver (v0.27+)
  --no-embedding        Defer embedding setup (skips the embedding-key check)
  --surface <verbs|starter|full>  Tool surface the printed harness registration pins, listed in full
                                  (default: starter, listing the memory verbs and request_tools)
  --search-mode <conservative|balanced|tokenmax>  Record the operator's search mode (no first-run ask; an existing brain's mode needs --force)
  --skip-embed-check    Skip the init-time embedding-key validation (config +
                        live test-embed). Also via GBRAIN_INIT_SKIP_EMBED_CHECK=1

EXAMPLES

content.text:
gbrain is set up as a free local memory for OpenClaw. It uses no API keys and no paid services, and it stays on this machine.

- **Brain:** I created it with gbrain's free defaults: a local database and no embedding provider (embeddings are what power meaning-based search). I saved a test fact and recalled it, which worked. `gbrain doctor` scores it 90/100, all checks OK. Its lower "brain score" comes from having no embeddings and an empty brain.
- **Connected to OpenClaw:** I registered gbrain as an MCP server for the main agent in `/harness-state/openclaw/openclaw.json`, under `mcp.servers.gbrain`. I added it alongside your existing settings and didn't change anything else. When I started the server by hand it listed `recall`, `remember`, `forget`, `entity`, `delta`, `synthesize`, `context_pack` and `request_tools`. I haven't confirmed the tools show up inside an OpenClaw session yet; a new session should have them.
- **PATH:** `~/.bashrc` and `~/.profile` didn't exist, so I created both with the Bun PATH line. `gbrain` now works in new shells.

**Settings gbrain chose (you can change them later):**
- **Search:** only exact keyword matching, with no meaning-based search. That's what keeping it free costs.
- **Search mode:** `conservative`, which keeps the amount of text fed back to the agent small.
- **Saving memories:** agents save only what you tell them to remember. gbrain recommends turning on automatic saving of facts you state: `gbrain config set memory.auto_writeback salient`.
- **Upkeep:** free background maintenance runs while a gbrain session is open. Nothing is deleted or charged without your say-so.
- **Conversation archive:** on. gbrain keeps one redacted page per agent conversation per day, stored locally. To turn it off: `gbrain transcripts archive off`.

The test fact "gbrain install check" is still in the brain. gbrain warns that deleting a fact saved this way withdraws it everywhere and means it can't be saved again, so I left it; it's harmless.
